bull_bear.body: Priorities stated as unchanged and in this order: invest in high-return growth, maintain balance sheet strength, return surplus cash to shareholders. Evidence this quarter: INR11/share first interim dividend paid; net cash of INR5,572cr maintained; INR6,450cr contributed to the national exchequer in taxes, royalties and duties. The dividend policy is unchanged at a minimum 30% of profit + 5% of reserves despite the Vedanta demerger — management was asked directly and confirmed no change. The pending INR24,000–25,000cr expansion decision in Q3 is the item that will test the "return surplus cash" leg.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Leadership transition.** Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash (ex-SAIL CMD, 30+ years in steel) on 1 August 2026; the CFO, Amit Gupta, is also newly appointed. A new CEO arrives precisely as a ~INR24,000cr capex decision reaches the board — strategy continuity is unproven.
- **Coal linkage failure.** 36% domestic linkage vs 64% a quarter ago is a real, unhedged cost exposure.
- **No hedging in FY27.** Management is deliberately unhedged given volatility; carried-forward positions (48kt zinc @ USD3,162, 34t silver @ USD63) sit well below spot, so they cost INR200cr in Q1 and will keep bleeding while prices stay high — but the unhedged book leaves earnings fully exposed to a price reversal.
- **Silver price moderation.** Silver fell to USD73/oz from the prior quarter's strong levels while contributing 46% of profit — the single largest earnings sensitivity.
- **SEBI observations on related-party transactions.** No penalty or restriction, but corrective measures were required. Root cause disclosed candidly: omnibus RPT approvals are set on *value*, and operating teams track *volume*, so a rising LME can breach the approved value. New SOP triggers an alarm at 80% of approved value with escalation to the Audit Committee.
- **GoI stake sale speculation.** Media reports of the government selling its ~27.92%; management deflected — "it is for the government to give the update."
- **Fertilizer plant regulatory risk.** Environmental clearance still pending; the Q1 FY28 date is contingent on it.
- **Silver WIP.** 10–15t of silver sitting in work-in-progress inflates the apparent Q1 shortfall against the 680t guide; if it does not unlock, the annual target is at risk.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Precise and willing to be pinned to numbers — 1.1mn tonnes was described as "our commitment," the 650KT capex was given as an honest straight-line extrapolation with the caveat that tendering would refine it, and the REE timeline was set at 2031–32 rather than sold as a near-term story. Arun Misra corrected two analyst framings cleanly: that the company had changed its no-concentrate-sale policy (it had not — this was legacy off-grade stock), and that the whole fertilizer plant commissions in Q2 (only phosphoric acid does). The RPT explanation was unusually transparent. Outgoing-CEO tone was valedictory; the CEO-designate did not speak on the call, which leaves the strategy-continuity question open.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The prepared remarks and the Q&A disagree on the fertilizer plant: the opening script said the Chanderiya fertilizer plant was "on track to be completed by the second quarter," while the CEO later said only phosphoric acid completes in Q2 and fertilizer slips to Q1 FY28. Take the Q&A version — and treat the script as evidence that timeline discipline needs watching under the new CEO.
- Sulphuric acid is doing quiet, structural work: prices up ~200% YoY, netted off COP, and royalty-free — it is simultaneously depressing reported COP *and* depressing royalty as a percentage of revenue. A normalisation in acid prices would hit the P&L twice over.
- The concentrate sale is the cleanest read on management's opportunism: rather than derate smelters with off-grade material, they sold legacy stock into a high-LME market for INR315cr. But they flagged they will *not* repeat it if it risks starving the smelters — so this revenue line should disappear.
- Q1 at 260kt against a 1.1mn tonne guide is already 1,040kt annualised, i.e. the guidance carries a built-in buffer that Q2–Q4 seasonality (Q4 typically 280–290kt) should comfortably clear. The guide looks conservative rather than stretched.
- Silver at 46% of profitability means this is no longer usefully modelled as a zinc company.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend policy is a minimum of 30% of profit after tax for the year or 5% of opening net worth, whichever is higher; the deck notes a paid dividend of Rs 11 per share (550% of face value, Rs 4,648 crore).
- Growth capital is committed only to projects clearing a >18% IRR hurdle, spanning capacity expansion, product diversification and critical-mineral blocks.
- Balance-sheet discipline framed around sustaining capex for existing operations, minimising working capital days, continuous sustainable cost reduction and retaining the AAA credit rating.
- Stated objective is maximising total shareholder return, with financial resilience through the commodity cycle presented as a core differentiator.

bull_bear.title: Management tone & governance (AGM 2026)

bull_bear.body:
- Structural cost leadership - first quartile of the global zinc mining cost curve and first decile of the global zinc smelting cost curve; FY2026 zinc cost of production (ex-royalty) of US$ 959 per tonne was a five-year low, better 9% YoY in dollar terms
- Full integration from ore body to end product and from captive power generation to customer delivery, so an advantage created in one part of the value chain reinforces the next
- Irreplaceable asset base - highest-ever ore R&R of 468.6 Mnt at an average zinc-lead grade of 6.2%, highest-ever metal reserve of 13.9 Mnt since the underground transition and record silver reserves of 10.9 kt, supporting 25+ years of mine life; world's 2nd largest zinc and lead reserves and resources base
- Dominant domestic position - India's only integrated and only primary zinc producer, with c.74% expected primary zinc market share and 600 kt of domestic zinc sales in FY2026
- India's only primary zinc alloy producer and only listed primary precious metal (silver) company, with value-added products at c.22% of sales (184 kt) and over 20x silver production growth over two decades
- Captive power with a rising renewable share - c.18% of the power mix from renewables in FY2026 and domestic coal use raised to 53%, insulating power cost from commodity price variation
- Industry-leading profitability cited by management - EBITDA margin of c.54% backed by operational excellence, technology, cost optimisation and better by-product realisation; c.67% return on capital employed and c.77% return on equity
- Consistently AAA credit rating by CRISIL, supporting funding for the growth phase
- Product and sustainability differentiation - EcoZen, Asia's first low-carbon zinc brand at under 1 tCO2e per tonne, commercially scaled in FY2026 with MoUs signed with Tata Steel and Silox India Limited
- Market-access and pricing transparency edge - 95% of sales through online price discovery in FY2026 against a 100% ambition, plus the January 2026 launch of Zinc Moolya, a rupee-linked live pricing module aimed at MSMEs
- ESG leadership as a commercial asset - ranked 1st in S&P Global CSA for the third consecutive year, first Indian member of ICMM, and Zinc Mark / Copper Mark certified sites
- Precious metals contributed c.45% of overall profitability, giving a second earnings engine alongside zinc
- Technology-led exploration - AI/ML targeting, drone-based surveys and 3D deposit modelling supporting continuous R&R replenishment
- Recognition by the market - inclusion in Nifty 100, Nifty Next 50 and the NSE F&O segment, and in the Nifty100 ESG, Nifty100 Enhanced ESG and Nifty100 ESG Sector Leaders indices
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price volatility across zinc, lead and silver — Earnings are directly exposed to LME/spot metal prices - management explicitly names 'hedging strategy: protection from price uncertainty' as an HZL 2.0 pillar and says it is 'strategically hedging some expected FY2027 volumes, to protect the balance sheet from pricing shocks'. The routed market data shows why: FY2026 zinc averaged US$ 2,970/t with a US$ 3,487/t peak, refined supply grew 4% YoY to 13.85 Mnt producing a marginal surplus, and LME (115 kt) and SHFE (149 kt) stocks left the market mostly in contango. Silver's all-time-high rally to US$ 118.45 per troy ounce in January 2026 lifted the precious portfolio to c.45% of profitability, which cuts both ways: a mix that concentrated in one volatile commodity is a structural exposure, not just a tailwind.
- Geopolitical realignment and trade-policy / tariff shock — The MD&A flags rising protectionism and aggressive US tariff hikes 'with some metals facing 50% duties' that have disrupted traditional trade routes, raised costs at global hubs, and created a policy-uncertainty climate 'weighing on global capital expenditure and trade volumes', with manufacturing PMIs hovering near the expansion/contraction boundary. Persistent tensions in the Middle East, Ukraine and Venezuela are disrupting energy supplies and driving commodity price volatility, and supply chains are shifting from just-in-time to 'just-in-case', making them more localised and expensive. This matters directly for the c.30% of refined zinc that is exported to South East Asia, the Middle East, the US and Europe, and for imported input costs.
- Short-seller allegations and open regulatory / authority enquiries — The statutory auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to Note 43 to the standalone financial statements 'regarding allegations made during the year by a short seller, and ongoing matters for which information has been sought by regulators/authorities, and Management's assessment thereof/responses thereto'. The opinion is not modified, but an unresolved regulatory enquiry is a live reputational, governance and potential-liability exposure that sits outside management's control and is the only matter the auditor chose to highlight.
- Cybersecurity, operational-technology and data-privacy risk — The Company devotes a full governance chapter to it: the Board's Audit and Risk Management Committee (chaired by Independent Director Ms. Pallavi Joshi Bakhru) has explicit oversight of enterprise cyber and technology risk, supported by a CEO-chaired IT and Cyber Security Steering Committee and a CISO reporting to the CFO, and the committee's charter covers 'cyber security risks, data privacy risks'. The disclosed control set - 24x7 SOC monitoring, cyber insurance and incident-response retainers for 'low-probability, high-impact cyberattacks', annual executive cyber drills and purple teaming, ISO 27001/22301/31000/27701 across 100% of Indian assets - is itself evidence of the exposure. The residual gap is named in the text: legacy operational technology and plant technical systems are still being upgraded in phases and a dedicated OT Security Operations Centre is only 'intended', so plant control systems remain the softest surface. Third-party and vendor access is a further named vector.
- Execution risk on the HZL 2.0 2x expansion and the standards that come with it — Management states the risk in its own words: 'delivering a 2x expansion, building a multi-metal future, scaling supporting capabilities, and meeting the expectations of ICMM would all require exceptional execution.' The programme is the largest expansion in the Company's history - nearly doubling refined metal capacity to 2.0 Mtpa - so slippage in project delivery, mine ramp-up or the parallel build-out of workforce capability would defer volume-led earnings growth while the capital is already committed. ICMM membership adds an external performance standard the Company must now be measured against.
- Cost of capital and financing conditions for a long-gestation capital programme — The MD&A warns that massive sovereign debt and geopolitical tension mean 'interest rates are unlikely to return to the ultra-low levels of the past decade' and that 'this new monetary paradigm necessitates agile financial strategies and selective capital allocation, particularly for long gestation sectors'. Mining and smelting expansion is precisely such a sector, so the funding environment for the multi-year growth programme is structurally tighter than in the previous cycle, even against a robust balance sheet.
- Safety exposure inherent to deep underground mining and smelting — Safety is described as 'non-negotiable' and is managed through a dedicated safety architecture - the Critical Risk Management programme and the Suraksha Kavach stewardship initiative - with technology being deployed specifically to remove people from hazardous environments (tele-remote drilling machines, remote mining operations from surface, robotic automation, AI-powered camera surveillance). The routed text also carries a footnote attributing a fatality to subsidiary Vedanta Zinc Football & Sports Foundation, confirming that fatal-incident risk extends across the group, not just the mines. For an operation running a 27,000+ workforce underground, a serious safety event carries human, regulatory and production-continuity consequences.
- Demand dependence on the galvanised-steel / industrial cycle and on Chinese supply behaviour — Zinc demand is concentrated in galvanising and construction-linked end uses, so the Company's volumes track the industrial and infrastructure cycle rather than a diversified customer base. The MD&A notes China's pivot away from infrastructure-heavy stimulus, weak Chinese real estate weighing on demand, and - on the supply side - that increased utilisation of China's new smelting capacity is expected to accumulate refined stocks and ease prices towards c.US$ 2,800 per tonne from CY2027. That combination means a demand slowdown and a supply-driven price reset could arrive together, in the same window as the expansion capex.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Zinc** — the volume engine; the 160,000 tpa roaster now absorbs incremental calcine demand during maintenance, plus debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba. Fundamentals described as supported by constrained mine supply and steady infrastructure/galvanization/battery demand.
- **Silver** — 46% of overall profitability, the single most important earnings driver. Price moderated to USD73/oz but management is constructive medium-term on solar, electronics and electrification demand against constrained supply. Mine development is being sequenced to hit higher-PPM silver ore, maximising in Q4.
- **Lead** — 149t silver production tracked lead production; planned lead smelter maintenance fell in Q1. Fundamentals "stable"; lead averaged USD1,954/t.
- **By-products** — sulphuric acid prices up ~200% YoY and carry **no mineral royalty** (not a mineral product), which is why royalty as a share of revenue is at multi-quarter lows. By-product realisation is netted off COP and was the reason Q1 beat the cost guidance.
- **Critical minerals / fertilizers** — REE+Yttrium block (Yttrium used in red-LED phosphors and medical applications); phosphoric acid → DAP fertilizer chain at Chanderiya, converting sulphuric acid into a higher-realisation product.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Cost leadership, quantified.** USD851/t zinc COP ex-royalty — the lowest since the underground transition and 16% below last year — against a guided band of USD975–1,000. The moat widened in a quarter when energy prices were rising.
- **Integration.** Mine-to-metal integration plus by-product recovery is what lets sulphuric acid at +200% prices and cadmium credits flow straight into the cost line; a non-integrated smelter cannot do this.
- **Grade and reserve base.** Rampura Agucha (world's largest zinc mine) and Sindesar Khurd underpin the fifth consecutive year of record Q1 mine metal.
- **Balance sheet as a competitive weapon.** Net cash INR5,572cr and INR5,253cr of pre-growth-capex FCF fund a INR24,000–25,000cr expansion without dilution or leverage stress.
- **Licence/ESG position.** Rampura Agucha became the first mine in India to receive Zinc Mark certification (after the Chanderiya smelter); first-time inclusion in the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Emerging Markets Index.

outlook.title: Strategic vision (the 5-year story) (AGM 2026)

outlook.body:
- HZL 2.0 - transform from a zinc-lead-silver producer into a larger, smarter, future-facing multi-metal critical-minerals enterprise, built on four pillars: scale (doubling refined metal capacity), getting smarter (digitalisation, automation, AI), diversification (entry into new critical minerals) and leading responsibly (scaling sustainability ambitions).
- Nearly double refined metal capacity from 1.144 Mtpa to 2.0 Mtpa through a predominantly brownfield, synchronised end-to-end build-up across mining, beneficiation and smelting, so that capacity ramps without operational bottlenecks.
- Defend and extend structural cost leadership through four levers management describes as built into the operating model: superior ore grades (an irreplicable geological advantage), energy cost optimisation (renewables plus higher domestic coal share), improved by-product realisation, and technology (AI, IIoT, automation) for equipment utilisation - with economies of scale from the expansion as an additional lever.
- Optimise the energy mix - raise renewable energy from c.18% of power requirement in FY2026 (c.13% in FY2025) towards 70% by FY2028 under the Serentica agreement, while re-engineering captive power plants to raise domestic coal use (53% in FY2026 vs 44% in FY2025).
- Diversify into new critical minerals where India is largely import-dependent - three new mineral blocks secured covering tungsten (Andhra Pradesh), rare earth elements (Uttar Pradesh) and potash (Rajasthan), positioning the Company within India's critical mineral mission and national self-reliance agenda.
- Sustain the resource base ahead of expansion - an exploration programme designed to hold mine life at 25+ years even after the capacity expansion, with metal reserves targeted to grow from 13.9 Mnt to 50 Mnt.
- Upgrade the product portfolio - expand value-added products (c.22% of sales, supported by the 30 ktpa zinc alloy plant at subsidiary HZAPL) and scale sustainable offerings such as EcoZen, Asia's first low-carbon zinc brand at under 1 tCO2e per tonne, with MoUs signed with Tata Steel and Silox India Limited.
- Build India's first integrated downstream ecosystem for zinc-based industries at the upcoming Zinc Park in Khankhala, Rajasthan, via MoUs with CMR Group and Tripura Group, supported by assured raw material supply.
- Strengthen market access and pricing transparency - progress from 95% towards 100% online price discovery sales, supported by Zinc Moolya, a rupee-linked live pricing module launched in January 2026 aimed at MSMEs.
- Disciplined risk management - strengthen cost leadership and strategically hedge some expected FY2027 volumes to protect the balance sheet from pricing shocks.
- Waste-to-wealth and circularity - convert Jarosite, manganese residue, sodium salt and calcium residue into commercially valuable products and dump waste in underground mines rather than transporting it to surface; commercialise legacy tailings via India's first tailings reprocessing plant.
- Scale digital and automation - a first-of-its-kind digital collaboration centre analysing data from all business units for real-time decisions, plus AI/ML, computer vision, video analytics and sensor fusion for switchyard hotspot monitoring, collision avoidance, human detection with crane interlocking, rock fragmentation analysis and chemical consumable optimisation; and open innovation through VSpark Deeptech Ventures with 30+ technology startups on 60+ projects.
- Unlock new revenue streams adjacent to the core - the DAP/NPK fertiliser plant using in-house sulphuric acid, and innovation in zinc-air batteries and zinc alloys for emerging applications.
- Lead responsibly against global benchmarks - ICMM membership (first Indian company; assessment already completed), Zinc Mark and Copper Mark certification at Chanderiya and Rampura Agucha, and the newly launched Sustainability Goals 2030 following early achievement of Sustainability Goals 2025.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The expansion story is 'HZL 2.0', a step-change programme whose scale pillar is doubling refined metal capacity to 2.0 Mtpa from the current 1.144 Mnt of refined metal capacity - described as the largest expansion in the Company's history, backed by disciplined capital allocation and proven execution capability. Its capacity-expansion headline in the MD&A is a '2x growth plan' anchored on 250 ktpa of integrated metal, alongside multi-metal diversification (new critical mineral blocks secured plus participation in further blocks), cost leadership through energy-mix optimisation, higher recovery and improved metal grades, and a hedging strategy for price protection. The build-out is executed mine by mine, with each asset carrying an explicit 'Enabling Hindustan Zinc's 2X growth plan' action list and an FY2029 ore-production target. Zawar Group of Mines (Mochia, Balaria, Zawarmala and Baroi; combined R&R base of 166 Mnt) targets 8.0 Mtpa of ore production capacity by FY2029, up from 4.8 Mtpa, through accelerated exploration and development of new mines, new beneficiation and paste-filling plants, rapid decline development and ventilation capacity build-up, and ramping Balaria and Baroi to 2.0 Mtpa. Rajpura Dariba Mine targets 6.0 Mtpa by FY2029, up from 2.0 Mtpa, via automation (tele-remote drilling, automated/remote pumping), a higher-capacity fleet (42 MT dump trucks, M2D development drills, tele-remote SIMBAs), decline development for East and South Lode mining with the mining partner already mobilised, and a next-generation material handling mechanism. A further mine, whose name is cut off in the routed text, targets 7.5 Mtpa by FY2029 up from 6.0 Mtpa by raising hoisting capacity from 3.75 Mtpa to 4.0 Mtpa with improved rate of descent to access new auxiliary lenses, expanding beneficiation capacity from 6.75 Mtpa to 7.5 Mtpa through debottlenecking of secondary crushing and grinding circuits, onboarding an expat production manager, and advanced tailings storage facility management. Underpinning all of it, exploration is focused on building towards over 500 Mnt of resources with 250 Mnt of reserves from the current 468.6 Mnt total R&R (25+ years of mine life), using AI/ML targeting, drone-based surveys and 3D deposit modelling; the mining footprint is eight world-class mines plus one new greenfield mine at Bamnia Kalan, all in Rajasthan. On the smelting side the report describes ongoing debottlenecking to unlock additional capacity across three smelters located adjacent to the mines plus the Pantnagar zinc-lead-silver refinery, and on power a 530 MW renewable energy power delivery agreement that will raise the renewable share of the power mix from c.18% to 70%. FY2026 itself delivered a heavy slate of asset-level commissioning: at Rajpura Dariba, India's first diesel-electric loader (17-tonne CAT-R2900XE), the new Maa Annapurna Portal enabling a larger cross-section decline and higher-capacity fleet (65 MT low-profile dump trucks, 21 MT LHDs), top-down mining with paste fill in the Main and East Lodes, paste-fill reticulation in the new E4 block, tele-remote SIMBA drilling machines, a dust extraction system at the secondary crusher, a 1 MVA dry-type transformer with fire detection and suppression for the main shaft winders, high-capacity remotely operated pumps at 11 mRL, IoT sensors on 11 critical equipment items and 28 Machine Max sensors; at Zawar, a 500 KW exhaust fan at Central Baroi lifting air capacity by 150 m3/s to 450 m3/s, the first remote surface operation of an underground pump at Mochia, Hindustan Zinc's longest raise of 600.2 m at Balaria, hydro filling at Balaria that will raise tailings utilisation from 17% to 25%, a shift to bulk emulsion charging, and new ore production from the Rawa area and 9E lens in the Mochia-Balaria cluster; and at Kayad, two ventilation fans (132 kW at +250 mRL and 450 kW at +120 mRL) boosting airflow by 150 m3/s. The rupee quantum of the programme is not narrated in this bundle; the only stated figures are the capital-commitment disclosures in the accounts.

outlook.body:
- Energy transition is the structural demand engine: management argues demand for zinc and silver 'is not cyclical' because every galvanised steel structure across wind, solar, transmission infrastructure and automobiles requires zinc, and every solar panel and semiconductor contains silver - framed as a decadal opportunity.
- Domestic tilt insulates the business from global volatility - around 70% of refined zinc and almost 100% of silver production is sold domestically, into what management calls one of the most constructive demand environments.
- India as the growth engine: FY2026 GDP growth projected at c.7.5% with retail inflation at a multi-year low of 2.75% in January 2026 and manufacturing PMI above 56 through most of the year (peaking at 59.3 in August 2025); various reports estimate FY2027 GDP growth of 6.4%-6.9%.
- Indian zinc consumption rose from 814 kt in CY2024 to 851 kt in CY2025, supported by Gati Shakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, strong steel and cement demand, road and rail modernisation, and IIP peaking at 7.8% growth in December 2025.
- India targeting 300 Mnt of crude steel capacity by 2030 under the National Steel Policy is expected to grow domestic zinc demand proportionately - management calls this the foundation for the plan to double capacity.
- Galvanising remains c.60% of first-use zinc demand (construction c.50%, transport c.21%, infrastructure c.16% by end use), with incremental demand from vehicle/die-cast production, appliances, power grid strengthening, transmission towers, solar mounting systems and wind structures.
- Zinc pricing backdrop: FY2026 prices averaged US$ 2,970 per tonne (+3% YoY) and peaked at US$ 3,487 per tonne, the highest since February 2023, on tight physical inventories and galvanising/infrastructure consumption. Per Wood Mackenzie, CY2026 demand is seen +1% YoY to 13.80 Mnt with mine supply falling 4.1% to 12.39 Mnt, prices averaging c.US$ 3,064 per tonne in CY2026 before easing towards c.US$ 2,800 per tonne from CY2027 as Chinese smelting capacity ramps; global mine output is expected to plateau by CY2028 and decline from CY2029.
- Silver re-rating: silver's inclusion in the US critical minerals list, combined with its dual identity as industrial input and safe-haven asset, drove a significant rally in FY2026; growing applications in solar cells, semiconductor chips, electronics and 5G networks.
- A 'split' metals market - energy-transition critical metals and precious metals are outperforming while traditional materials such as iron ore face downward pressure, as China pivots from infrastructure-heavy stimulus to consumption.
- Supply-side discipline is structurally supportive - major miners are prioritising dividends and acquisitions over risky greenfield development, keeping supply tight for critical minerals and treatment charges consistently low.
- Margin lever - cost of production: FY2026 zinc COP (ex-royalty) fell 9% to US$ 959 per tonne on renewables share, domestic coal share, by-product realisation and technology; management says it is 'confident of sustaining the cost of production' while also benefiting from economies of scale as capacity expands.
- Mix lever - value-added products at c.22% of sales and precious metals contributing c.45% of profitability, with the zinc alloy plant and EcoZen extending the premium portfolio.
- FY2027 stance: 'a phase of cautious optimism' - the global economic environment may remain tepid on geopolitical uncertainty, but commodity markets are expected to offer upside potential from steady demand in key downstream industries, with India supported by sustained infrastructure investment, rising steel demand and expansion in industrial activity.
- Headwinds flagged in the operating environment - US tariff hikes (some metals facing 50% duties), a shift from just-in-time to just-in-case supply chains raising costs, interest rates unlikely to return to ultra-low levels (necessitating selective capital allocation for long-gestation projects), and a marginal refined zinc surplus with LME stocks at 115 kt and SHFE at 149 kt as of March 31, 2026 leaving the market mostly in contango.
- Deglobalisation and resource nationalism are treated as an opportunity, not just a risk - India's critical mineral mission and the global push to reduce dependence on concentrated supply chains are described as tailwinds for India's only primary zinc-lead-silver producer.
- The HZL 2.0 programme itself is presented as the earnings driver - expected to drive volume-led earnings growth, improve asset utilisation and strengthen cash flow generation.

currentContext.expansion: The expansion story is 'HZL 2.0', a step-change programme whose scale pillar is doubling refined metal capacity to 2.0 Mtpa from the current 1.144 Mnt of refined metal capacity - described as the largest expansion in the Company's history, backed by disciplined capital allocation and proven execution capability. Its capacity-expansion headline in the MD&A is a '2x growth plan' anchored on 250 ktpa of integrated metal, alongside multi-metal diversification (new critical mineral blocks secured plus participation in further blocks), cost leadership through energy-mix optimisation, higher recovery and improved metal grades, and a hedging strategy for price protection. The build-out is executed mine by mine, with each asset carrying an explicit 'Enabling Hindustan Zinc's 2X growth plan' action list and an FY2029 ore-production target. Zawar Group of Mines (Mochia, Balaria, Zawarmala and Baroi; combined R&R base of 166 Mnt) targets 8.0 Mtpa of ore production capacity by FY2029, up from 4.8 Mtpa, through accelerated exploration and development of new mines, new beneficiation and paste-filling plants, rapid decline development and ventilation capacity build-up, and ramping Balaria and Baroi to 2.0 Mtpa. Rajpura Dariba Mine targets 6.0 Mtpa by FY2029, up from 2.0 Mtpa, via automation (tele-remote drilling, automated/remote pumping), a higher-capacity fleet (42 MT dump trucks, M2D development drills, tele-remote SIMBAs), decline development for East and South Lode mining with the mining partner already mobilised, and a next-generation material handling mechanism. A further mine, whose name is cut off in the routed text, targets 7.5 Mtpa by FY2029 up from 6.0 Mtpa by raising hoisting capacity from 3.75 Mtpa to 4.0 Mtpa with improved rate of descent to access new auxiliary lenses, expanding beneficiation capacity from 6.75 Mtpa to 7.5 Mtpa through debottlenecking of secondary crushing and grinding circuits, onboarding an expat production manager, and advanced tailings storage facility management. Underpinning all of it, exploration is focused on building towards over 500 Mnt of resources with 250 Mnt of reserves from the current 468.6 Mnt total R&R (25+ years of mine life), using AI/ML targeting, drone-based surveys and 3D deposit modelling; the mining footprint is eight world-class mines plus one new greenfield mine at Bamnia Kalan, all in Rajasthan. On the smelting side the report describes ongoing debottlenecking to unlock additional capacity across three smelters located adjacent to the mines plus the Pantnagar zinc-lead-silver refinery, and on power a 530 MW renewable energy power delivery agreement that will raise the renewable share of the power mix from c.18% to 70%. FY2026 itself delivered a heavy slate of asset-level commissioning: at Rajpura Dariba, India's first diesel-electric loader (17-tonne CAT-R2900XE), the new Maa Annapurna Portal enabling a larger cross-section decline and higher-capacity fleet (65 MT low-profile dump trucks, 21 MT LHDs), top-down mining with paste fill in the Main and East Lodes, paste-fill reticulation in the new E4 block, tele-remote SIMBA drilling machines, a dust extraction system at the secondary crusher, a 1 MVA dry-type transformer with fire detection and suppression for the main shaft winders, high-capacity remotely operated pumps at 11 mRL, IoT sensors on 11 critical equipment items and 28 Machine Max sensors; at Zawar, a 500 KW exhaust fan at Central Baroi lifting air capacity by 150 m3/s to 450 m3/s, the first remote surface operation of an underground pump at Mochia, Hindustan Zinc's longest raise of 600.2 m at Balaria, hydro filling at Balaria that will raise tailings utilisation from 17% to 25%, a shift to bulk emulsion charging, and new ore production from the Rawa area and 9E lens in the Mochia-Balaria cluster; and at Kayad, two ventilation fans (132 kW at +250 mRL and 450 kW at +120 mRL) boosting airflow by 150 m3/s. The rupee quantum of the programme is not narrated in this bundle; the only stated figures are the capital-commitment disclosures in the accounts.
currentContext.mdna: Energy transition is the structural demand engine: management argues demand for zinc and silver 'is not cyclical' because every galvanised steel structure across wind, solar, transmission infrastructure and automobiles requires zinc, and every solar panel and semiconductor contains silver - framed as a decadal opportunity.|Domestic tilt insulates the business from global volatility - around 70% of refined zinc and almost 100% of silver production is sold domestically, into what management calls one of the most constructive demand environments.|India as the growth engine: FY2026 GDP growth projected at c.7.5% with retail inflation at a multi-year low of 2.75% in January 2026 and manufacturing PMI above 56 through most of the year (peaking at 59.3 in August 2025); various reports estimate FY2027 GDP growth of 6.4%-6.9%.|Indian zinc consumption rose from 814 kt in CY2024 to 851 kt in CY2025, supported by Gati Shakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, strong steel and cement demand, road and rail modernisation, and IIP peaking at 7.8% growth in December 2025.|India targeting 300 Mnt of crude steel capacity by 2030 under the National Steel Policy is expected to grow domestic zinc demand proportionately - management calls this the foundation for the plan to double capacity.|Galvanising remains c.60% of first-use zinc demand (construction c.50%, transport c.21%, infrastructure c.16% by end use), with incremental demand from vehicle/die-cast production, appliances, power grid strengthening, transmission towers, solar mounting systems and wind structures.|Zinc pricing backdrop: FY2026 prices averaged US$ 2,970 per tonne (+3% YoY) and peaked at US$ 3,487 per tonne, the highest since February 2023, on tight physical inventories and galvanising/infrastructure consumption. global mine output is expected to plateau by CY2028 and decline from CY2029.|Silver re-rating: silver's inclusion in the US critical minerals list, combined with its dual identity as industrial input and safe-haven asset, drove a significant rally in FY2026; risks.risk: Commodity price volatility across zinc, lead and silver
risks.note: Earnings are directly exposed to LME/spot metal prices - management explicitly names 'hedging strategy: protection from price uncertainty' as an HZL 2.0 pillar and says it is 'strategically hedging some expected FY2027 volumes, to protect the balance sheet from pricing shocks'. The routed market data shows why: FY2026 zinc averaged US$ 2,970/t with a US$ 3,487/t peak, refined supply grew 4% YoY to 13.85 Mnt producing a marginal surplus, and LME (115 kt) and SHFE (149 kt) stocks left the market mostly in contango. Silver's all-time-high rally to US$ 118.45 per troy ounce in January 2026 lifted the precious portfolio to c.45% of profitability, which cuts both ways: a mix that concentrated in one volatile commodity is a structural exposure, not just a tailwind.

risks.risk: Geopolitical realignment and trade-policy / tariff shock
risks.note: The MD&A flags rising protectionism and aggressive US tariff hikes 'with some metals facing 50% duties' that have disrupted traditional trade routes, raised costs at global hubs, and created a policy-uncertainty climate 'weighing on global capital expenditure and trade volumes', with manufacturing PMIs hovering near the expansion/contraction boundary. Persistent tensions in the Middle East, Ukraine and Venezuela are disrupting energy supplies and driving commodity price volatility, and supply chains are shifting from just-in-time to 'just-in-case', making them more localised and expensive. This matters directly for the c.30% of refined zinc that is exported to South East Asia, the Middle East, the US and Europe, and for imported input costs.

risks.risk: Short-seller allegations and open regulatory / authority enquiries
risks.note: The statutory auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to Note 43 to the standalone financial statements 'regarding allegations made during the year by a short seller, and ongoing matters for which information has been sought by regulators/authorities, and Management's assessment thereof/responses thereto'. The opinion is not modified, but an unresolved regulatory enquiry is a live reputational, governance and potential-liability exposure that sits outside management's control and is the only matter the auditor chose to highlight.

The Company devotes a full governance chapter to it: the Board's Audit and Risk Management Committee (chaired by Independent Director Ms. Pallavi Joshi Bakhru) has explicit oversight of enterprise cyber and technology risk, supported by a CEO-chaired IT and Cyber Security Steering Committee and a CISO reporting to the CFO, and the committee's charter covers 'cyber security risks, data privacy risks'. The disclosed control set - 24x7 SOC monitoring, cyber insurance and incident-response retainers for 'low-probability, high-impact cyberattacks', annual executive cyber drills and purple teaming, ISO 27001/22301/31000/27701 across 100% of Indian assets - is itself evidence of the exposure. The residual gap is named in the text: legacy operational technology and plant technical systems are still being upgraded in phases and a dedicated OT Security Operations Centre is only 'intended', so plant control systems remain the softest surface. Third-party and vendor access is a further named vector.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the HZL 2.0 2x expansion and the standards that come with it
risks.note: Management states the risk in its own words: 'delivering a 2x expansion, building a multi-metal future, scaling supporting capabilities, and meeting the expectations of ICMM would all require exceptional execution.' The programme is the largest expansion in the Company's history - nearly doubling refined metal capacity to 2.0 Mtpa - so slippage in project delivery, mine ramp-up or the parallel build-out of workforce capability would defer volume-led earnings growth while the capital is already committed. ICMM membership adds an external performance standard the Company must now be measured against.

risks.risk: Cost of capital and financing conditions for a long-gestation capital programme
risks.note: The MD&A warns that massive sovereign debt and geopolitical tension mean 'interest rates are unlikely to return to the ultra-low levels of the past decade' and that 'this new monetary paradigm necessitates agile financial strategies and selective capital allocation, particularly for long gestation sectors'. Mining and smelting expansion is precisely such a sector, so the funding environment for the multi-year growth programme is structurally tighter than in the previous cycle, even against a robust balance sheet.

risks.risk: Safety exposure inherent to deep underground mining and smelting
risks.note: Safety is described as 'non-negotiable' and is managed through a dedicated safety architecture - the Critical Risk Management programme and the Suraksha Kavach stewardship initiative - with technology being deployed specifically to remove people from hazardous environments (tele-remote drilling machines, remote mining operations from surface, robotic automation, AI-powered camera surveillance). The routed text also carries a footnote attributing a fatality to subsidiary Vedanta Zinc Football & Sports Foundation, confirming that fatal-incident risk extends across the group, not just the mines. For an operation running a 27,000+ workforce underground, a serious safety event carries human, regulatory and production-continuity consequences.

risks.risk: Demand dependence on the galvanised-steel / industrial cycle and on Chinese supply behaviour
risks.note: Zinc demand is concentrated in galvanising and construction-linked end uses, so the Company's volumes track the industrial and infrastructure cycle rather than a diversified customer base. The MD&A notes China's pivot away from infrastructure-heavy stimulus, weak Chinese real estate weighing on demand, and - on the supply side - that increased utilisation of China's new smelting capacity is expected to accumulate refined stocks and ease prices towards c.US$ 2,800 per tonne from CY2027. That combination means a demand slowdown and a supply-driven price reset could arrive together, in the same window as the expansion capex.

one-line thesis: An all-time record quarter on every line — revenue INR13,747cr (+77%), EBITDA INR8,074cr (+109%, first time above INR8,000cr), PAT INR5,469cr (+145%) — produced by the rare combination of the lowest zinc cost of production since the underground transition (USD851/t, −16% YoY) *and* a commodity price tailwind, with silver alone contributing 46% of profitability. Behind the numbers sits a leadership handover (Arun Misra out, ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash in from 1 August) and a capital-allocation decision point: a ~650KT smelter+mine expansion costing roughly INR24,000–25,000cr goes to the board in Q3 FY27.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Volume:** **1.1 million tonnes refined metal for FY27** — reaffirmed twice and explicitly called "our commitment." Q1 at 260kt; Q2 must "cross around 280 KT"; Q4 historically touches 280–290kt. **Silver 680 t for FY27** — implies ~175t/quarter for the remaining three; management said achieving it "will not be difficult" on better mine grades.

order book & pipeline: Not applicable (commodity producer). The project pipeline is the forward book — see §8. The mineral-resource pipeline gained a rare-earth-elements and Yttrium block at Gundlupet, Karnataka, secured this quarter at G2 exploration level.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Zinc** — the volume engine; the 160,000 tpa roaster now absorbs incremental calcine demand during maintenance, plus debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba. Fundamentals described as supported by constrained mine supply and steady infrastructure/galvanization/battery demand.
- **Silver** — 46% of overall profitability, the single most important earnings driver. Price moderated to USD73/oz but management is constructive medium-term on solar, electronics and electrification demand against constrained supply. Mine development is being sequenced to hit higher-PPM silver ore, maximising in Q4.
- **Lead** — 149t silver production tracked lead production; planned lead smelter maintenance fell in Q1. Fundamentals "stable"; lead averaged USD1,954/t.
- **By-products** — sulphuric acid prices up ~200% YoY and carry **no mineral royalty** (not a mineral product), which is why royalty as a share of revenue is at multi-quarter lows. By-product realisation is netted off COP and was the reason Q1 beat the cost guidance.
- **Critical minerals / fertilizers** — REE+Yttrium block (Yttrium used in red-LED phosphors and medical applications); phosphoric acid → DAP fertilizer chain at Chanderiya, converting sulphuric acid into a higher-realisation product.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **2X growth journey** — the ~650KT smelter+mine conceptualisation is its concrete expression; the Q3 FY27 board decision is the checkpoint.
- **Tailings reprocessing** — genuinely novel: management said only one mine in Australia has done it at this scale, which is why a 6–8 month ramp is assumed rather than a standard curve. 30–35kt of zinc recovered from waste is high-margin volume.
- **Critical minerals diversification** — REE/Yttrium is a decade-out option, not a near-term earnings item; management was explicit about that.
- **Fertilizers** — phosphoric acid first (Q2 FY27), DAP later (Q1 FY28).
- **Renewables** — RE consumption at 22% of energy and rising; a direct COP lever given the coal linkage shortfall. MoUs signed with Advantek Associates LLP and Aero Eagle Automobile Pvt Ltd on green hydrogen and clean energy. India's first 250-tonne electric crane deployed.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Cost leadership, quantified.** USD851/t zinc COP ex-royalty — the lowest since the underground transition and 16% below last year — against a guided band of USD975–1,000. The moat widened in a quarter when energy prices were rising.
- **Integration.** Mine-to-metal integration plus by-product recovery is what lets sulphuric acid at +200% prices and cadmium credits flow straight into the cost line; a non-integrated smelter cannot do this.
- **Grade and reserve base.** Rampura Agucha (world's largest zinc mine) and Sindesar Khurd underpin the fifth consecutive year of record Q1 mine metal.
- **Balance sheet as a competitive weapon.** Net cash INR5,572cr and INR5,253cr of pre-growth-capex FCF fund a INR24,000–25,000cr expansion without dilution or leverage stress.
- **Licence/ESG position.** Rampura Agucha became the first mine in India to receive Zinc Mark certification (after the Chanderiya smelter); first-time inclusion in the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Emerging Markets Index.
margins & cost dynamics: The 59% EBITDA margin is the output of three stacked effects: record volume, record-low COP, and a price/currency tailwind. Management's COP bridge: better grades, higher metal production, higher renewable power share and better by-product realisation, **partly offset by higher input commodity prices, especially energy**. The one deteriorating input is coal — domestic linkage materialisation collapsed to 36% from 64% in Q4, pushing the mix to costlier imported coal, which is why power & fuel rose sequentially *despite* lower production and a higher RE share. Management expects Q2 COP to improve as volumes rise above 280kt (fixed-cost dilution) and acid credits persist, but explicitly caveated "unless we are struck by higher input commodity prices, which is also a likelihood."

capital allocation: Priorities stated as unchanged and in this order: invest in high-return growth, maintain balance sheet strength, return surplus cash to shareholders. Evidence this quarter: INR11/share first interim dividend paid; net cash of INR5,572cr maintained; INR6,450cr contributed to the national exchequer in taxes, royalties and duties. The dividend policy is unchanged at a minimum 30% of profit + 5% of reserves despite the Vedanta demerger — management was asked directly and confirmed no change. The pending INR24,000–25,000cr expansion decision in Q3 is the item that will test the "return surplus cash" leg.
risks & watch-items:
- **Leadership transition.** Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash (ex-SAIL CMD, 30+ years in steel) on 1 August 2026; the CFO, Amit Gupta, is also newly appointed. A new CEO arrives precisely as a ~INR24,000cr capex decision reaches the board — strategy continuity is unproven.
- **Coal linkage failure.** 36% domestic linkage vs 64% a quarter ago is a real, unhedged cost exposure.
- **No hedging in FY27.** Management is deliberately unhedged given volatility; carried-forward positions (48kt zinc @ USD3,162, 34t silver @ USD63) sit well below spot, so they cost INR200cr in Q1 and will keep bleeding while prices stay high — but the unhedged book leaves earnings fully exposed to a price reversal.
- **Silver price moderation.** Silver fell to USD73/oz from the prior quarter's strong levels while contributing 46% of profit — the single largest earnings sensitivity.
- **SEBI observations on related-party transactions.** No penalty or restriction, but corrective measures were required. Root cause disclosed candidly: omnibus RPT approvals are set on *value*, and operating teams track *volume*, so a rising LME can breach the approved value. New SOP triggers an alarm at 80% of approved value with escalation to the Audit Committee.
- **GoI stake sale speculation.** Media reports of the government selling its ~27.92%; management deflected — "it is for the government to give the update."
- **Fertilizer plant regulatory risk.** Environmental clearance still pending; the Q1 FY28 date is contingent on it.
- **Silver WIP.** 10–15t of silver sitting in work-in-progress inflates the apparent Q1 shortfall against the 680t guide; if it does not unlock, the annual target is at risk.
management quality / tone: Precise and willing to be pinned to numbers — 1.1mn tonnes was described as "our commitment," the 650KT capex was given as an honest straight-line extrapolation with the caveat that tendering would refine it, and the REE timeline was set at 2031–32 rather than sold as a near-term story. Arun Misra corrected two analyst framings cleanly: that the company had changed its no-concentrate-sale policy (it had not — this was legacy off-grade stock), and that the whole fertilizer plant commissions in Q2 (only phosphoric acid does). The RPT explanation was unusually transparent. Outgoing-CEO tone was valedictory; the CEO-designate did not speak on the call, which leaves the strategy-continuity question open.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The prepared remarks and the Q&A disagree on the fertilizer plant: the opening script said the Chanderiya fertilizer plant was "on track to be completed by the second quarter," while the CEO later said only phosphoric acid completes in Q2 and fertilizer slips to Q1 FY28. Take the Q&A version — and treat the script as evidence that timeline discipline needs watching under the new CEO.
- Sulphuric acid is doing quiet, structural work: prices up ~200% YoY, netted off COP, and royalty-free — it is simultaneously depressing reported COP *and* depressing royalty as a percentage of revenue. A normalisation in acid prices would hit the P&L twice over.
- The concentrate sale is the cleanest read on management's opportunism: rather than derate smelters with off-grade material, they sold legacy stock into a high-LME market for INR315cr. But they flagged they will *not* repeat it if it risks starving the smelters — so this revenue line should disappear.
- Q1 at 260kt against a 1.1mn tonne guide is already 1,040kt annualised, i.e. the guidance carries a built-in buffer that Q2–Q4 seasonality (Q4 typically 280–290kt) should comfortably clear. The guide looks conservative rather than stretched.
- Silver at 46% of profitability means this is no longer usefully modelled as a zinc company.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: A subsidiary of Vedanta Limited and headquartered in Udaipur, Rajasthan, Hindustan Zinc mines and smelts zinc, lead and silver through a fully integrated chain that runs from its own ore bodies in Rajasthan to refined metal, backed by captive power. Its product portfolio spans refined zinc, lead and silver plus value-added products such as continuous galvanising grade (CGG) zinc, special high grade (SHG) jumbos, die-cast alloys and zinc alloys, sold to galvanisers, steel, automotive, infrastructure, battery and electronics customers in India and 40+ countries. With over 60 years of operating experience, a 468.6 Mnt R&R base at an average zinc-lead grade of 6.2% and 25+ years of mine life, the Company is now pursuing 'HZL 2.0' - doubling refined metal capacity and diversifying into new critical minerals.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Zinc** — the volume engine; the 160,000 tpa roaster now absorbs incremental calcine demand during maintenance, plus debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba. Fundamentals described as supported by constrained mine supply and steady infrastructure/galvanization/battery demand.
- **Silver** — 46% of overall profitability, the single most important earnings driver. Price moderated to USD73/oz but management is constructive medium-term on solar, electronics and electrification demand against constrained supply. Mine development is being sequenced to hit higher-PPM silver ore, maximising in Q4.
- **Lead** — 149t silver production tracked lead production; planned lead smelter maintenance fell in Q1. Fundamentals "stable"; lead averaged USD1,954/t.
- **By-products** — sulphuric acid prices up ~200% YoY and carry **no mineral royalty** (not a mineral product), which is why royalty as a share of revenue is at multi-quarter lows. By-product realisation is netted off COP and was the reason Q1 beat the cost guidance.
- **Critical minerals / fertilizers** — REE+Yttrium block (Yttrium used in red-LED phosphors and medical applications); phosphoric acid → DAP fertilizer chain at Chanderiya, converting sulphuric acid into a higher-realisation product.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Volume:** **1.1 million tonnes refined metal for FY27** — reaffirmed twice and explicitly called "our commitment." Q1 at 260kt; Q2 must "cross around 280 KT"; Q4 historically touches 280–290kt. **Silver 680 t for FY27** — implies ~175t/quarter for the remaining three; management said achieving it "will not be difficult" on better mine grades.
- **Cost:** zinc COP ex-royalty guidance held at **USD975–1,000/t** for FY27; Q1's USD851 beat it on superior by-product realisation. Management expects Q2 cost to improve further if volumes rise and sulphuric acid prices (up ~200% YoY) hold.
- **Margin:** no explicit margin target; the guided mechanism is volume-driven cost dilution.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:**
  - FY27 growth capex **USD500–600 million**.
  - **Phosphoric acid plant (Chanderiya) — commissioning in Q2 FY27.** Note: prepared remarks said the "fertilizer plant at Chanderiya" was on track for Q2; under questioning the CEO clarified only the *phosphoric acid* portion completes in Q2.
  - **Fertilizer (DAP) plant — Q1 FY28**, gated on pending environmental clearance and regulatory approvals. ~INR500cr already spent.
  - **Hot acid leaching plant, Dariba — Q2 FY27.**
  - **Tailings reprocessing plant — construction just started, ~24 months to build**, then a **6–8 month ramp**; expected output **30–35 kt of zinc**.
  - **250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter, Debari** — mine development started to match mining capacity.
  - **~650 KT new smelter + mine complex — board approval targeted in Q3 FY27, then 36 months construction; indicative capex INR24,000–25,000 cr** (extrapolated from ~INR12,000cr for 250kt; tendering underway, firm number expected in ~1 month).
  - **REE/Yttrium (Gundlupet)** — 2–3 years exploration, first production only around **2031–32**.
- **Balance sheet:** to remain a **net cash company at FY27 exit**.
- **Dividend:** policy unchanged — **minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves**.
- **Operations:** **no further smelter shutdowns or planned maintenance for the remainder of FY27.**

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **2X growth journey** — the ~650KT smelter+mine conceptualisation is its concrete expression; the Q3 FY27 board decision is the checkpoint.
- **Tailings reprocessing** — genuinely novel: management said only one mine in Australia has done it at this scale, which is why a 6–8 month ramp is assumed rather than a standard curve. 30–35kt of zinc recovered from waste is high-margin volume.
- **Critical minerals diversification** — REE/Yttrium is a decade-out option, not a near-term earnings item; management was explicit about that.
- **Fertilizers** — phosphoric acid first (Q2 FY27), DAP later (Q1 FY28).
- **Renewables** — RE consumption at 22% of energy and rising; a direct COP lever given the coal linkage shortfall. MoUs signed with Advantek Associates LLP and Aero Eagle Automobile Pvt Ltd on green hydrogen and clean energy. India's first 250-tonne electric crane deployed.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Energy transition is the structural demand engine: management argues demand for zinc and silver 'is not cyclical' because every galvanised steel structure across wind, solar, transmission infrastructure and automobiles requires zinc, and every solar panel and semiconductor contains silver - framed as a decadal opportunity.
- Domestic tilt insulates the business from global volatility - around 70% of refined zinc and almost 100% of silver production is sold domestically, into what management calls one of the most constructive demand environments.
- India as the growth engine: FY2026 GDP growth projected at c.7.5% with retail inflation at a multi-year low of 2.75% in January 2026 and manufacturing PMI above 56 through most of the year (peaking at 59.3 in August 2025); various reports estimate FY2027 GDP growth of 6.4%-6.9%.
- Indian zinc consumption rose from 814 kt in CY2024 to 851 kt in CY2025, supported by Gati Shakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, strong steel and cement demand, road and rail modernisation, and IIP peaking at 7.8% growth in December 2025.
- India targeting 300 Mnt of crude steel capacity by 2030 under the National Steel Policy is expected to grow domestic zinc demand proportionately - management calls this the foundation for the plan to double capacity.
- Galvanising remains c.60% of first-use zinc demand (construction c.50%, transport c.21%, infrastructure c.16% by end use), with incremental demand from vehicle/die-cast production, appliances, power grid strengthening, transmission towers, solar mounting systems and wind structures.
- Zinc pricing backdrop: FY2026 prices averaged US$ 2,970 per tonne (+3% YoY) and peaked at US$ 3,487 per tonne, the highest since February 2023, on tight physical inventories and galvanising/infrastructure consumption. Per Wood Mackenzie, CY2026 demand is seen +1% YoY to 13.80 Mnt with mine supply falling 4.1% to 12.39 Mnt, prices averaging c.US$ 3,064 per tonne in CY2026 before easing towards c.US$ 2,800 per tonne from CY2027 as Chinese smelting capacity ramps; global mine output is expected to plateau by CY2028 and decline from CY2029.
- Silver re-rating: silver's inclusion in the US critical minerals list, combined with its dual identity as industrial input and safe-haven asset, drove a significant rally in FY2026; growing applications in solar cells, semiconductor chips, electronics and 5G networks.
- A 'split' metals market - energy-transition critical metals and precious metals are outperforming while traditional materials such as iron ore face downward pressure, as China pivots from infrastructure-heavy stimulus to consumption.
- Supply-side discipline is structurally supportive - major miners are prioritising dividends and acquisitions over risky greenfield development, keeping supply tight for critical minerals and treatment charges consistently low.
- Margin lever - cost of production: FY2026 zinc COP (ex-royalty) fell 9% to US$ 959 per tonne on renewables share, domestic coal share, by-product realisation and technology; management says it is 'confident of sustaining the cost of production' while also benefiting from economies of scale as capacity expands.
- Mix lever - value-added products at c.22% of sales and precious metals contributing c.45% of profitability, with the zinc alloy plant and EcoZen extending the premium portfolio.
- FY2027 stance: 'a phase of cautious optimism' - the global economic environment may remain tepid on geopolitical uncertainty, but commodity markets are expected to offer upside potential from steady demand in key downstream industries, with India supported by sustained infrastructure investment, rising steel demand and expansion in industrial activity.
- Headwinds flagged in the operating environment - US tariff hikes (some metals facing 50% duties), a shift from just-in-time to just-in-case supply chains raising costs, interest rates unlikely to return to ultra-low levels (necessitating selective capital allocation for long-gestation projects), and a marginal refined zinc surplus with LME stocks at 115 kt and SHFE at 149 kt as of March 31, 2026 leaving the market mostly in contango.
- Deglobalisation and resource nationalism are treated as an opportunity, not just a risk - India's critical mineral mission and the global push to reduce dependence on concentrated supply chains are described as tailwinds for India's only primary zinc-lead-silver producer.
- The HZL 2.0 programme itself is presented as the earnings driver - expected to drive volume-led earnings growth, improve asset utilisation and strengthen cash flow generation.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: The 59% EBITDA margin is the output of three stacked effects: record volume, record-low COP, and a price/currency tailwind. Management's COP bridge: better grades, higher metal production, higher renewable power share and better by-product realisation, **partly offset by higher input commodity prices, especially energy**. The one deteriorating input is coal — domestic linkage materialisation collapsed to 36% from 64% in Q4, pushing the mix to costlier imported coal, which is why power & fuel rose sequentially *despite* lower production and a higher RE share. Management expects Q2 COP to improve as volumes rise above 280kt (fixed-cost dilution) and acid credits persist, but explicitly caveated "unless we are struck by higher input commodity prices, which is also a likelihood."

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priorities stated as unchanged and in this order: invest in high-return growth, maintain balance sheet strength, return surplus cash to shareholders. Evidence this quarter: INR11/share first interim dividend paid; net cash of INR5,572cr maintained; INR6,450cr contributed to the national exchequer in taxes, royalties and duties. The dividend policy is unchanged at a minimum 30% of profit + 5% of reserves despite the Vedanta demerger — management was asked directly and confirmed no change. The pending INR24,000–25,000cr expansion decision in Q3 is the item that will test the "return surplus cash" leg.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The expansion story is 'HZL 2.0', a step-change programme whose scale pillar is doubling refined metal capacity to 2.0 Mtpa from the current 1.144 Mnt of refined metal capacity - described as the largest expansion in the Company's history, backed by disciplined capital allocation and proven execution capability. Its capacity-expansion headline in the MD&A is a '2x growth plan' anchored on 250 ktpa of integrated metal, alongside multi-metal diversification (new critical mineral blocks secured plus participation in further blocks), cost leadership through energy-mix optimisation, higher recovery and improved metal grades, and a hedging strategy for price protection. The build-out is executed mine by mine, with each asset carrying an explicit 'Enabling Hindustan Zinc's 2X growth plan' action list and an FY2029 ore-production target. Zawar Group of Mines (Mochia, Balaria, Zawarmala and Baroi; combined R&R base of 166 Mnt) targets 8.0 Mtpa of ore production capacity by FY2029, up from 4.8 Mtpa, through accelerated exploration and development of new mines, new beneficiation and paste-filling plants, rapid decline development and ventilation capacity build-up, and ramping Balaria and Baroi to 2.0 Mtpa. Rajpura Dariba Mine targets 6.0 Mtpa by FY2029, up from 2.0 Mtpa, via automation (tele-remote drilling, automated/remote pumping), a higher-capacity fleet (42 MT dump trucks, M2D development drills, tele-remote SIMBAs), decline development for East and South Lode mining with the mining partner already mobilised, and a next-generation material handling mechanism. A further mine, whose name is cut off in the routed text, targets 7.5 Mtpa by FY2029 up from 6.0 Mtpa by raising hoisting capacity from 3.75 Mtpa to 4.0 Mtpa with improved rate of descent to access new auxiliary lenses, expanding beneficiation capacity from 6.75 Mtpa to 7.5 Mtpa through debottlenecking of secondary crushing and grinding circuits, onboarding an expat production manager, and advanced tailings storage facility management. Underpinning all of it, exploration is focused on building towards over 500 Mnt of resources with 250 Mnt of reserves from the current 468.6 Mnt total R&R (25+ years of mine life), using AI/ML targeting, drone-based surveys and 3D deposit modelling; the mining footprint is eight world-class mines plus one new greenfield mine at Bamnia Kalan, all in Rajasthan. On the smelting side the report describes ongoing debottlenecking to unlock additional capacity across three smelters located adjacent to the mines plus the Pantnagar zinc-lead-silver refinery, and on power a 530 MW renewable energy power delivery agreement that will raise the renewable share of the power mix from c.18% to 70%. FY2026 itself delivered a heavy slate of asset-level commissioning: at Rajpura Dariba, India's first diesel-electric loader (17-tonne CAT-R2900XE), the new Maa Annapurna Portal enabling a larger cross-section decline and higher-capacity fleet (65 MT low-profile dump trucks, 21 MT LHDs), top-down mining with paste fill in the Main and East Lodes, paste-fill reticulation in the new E4 block, tele-remote SIMBA drilling machines, a dust extraction system at the secondary crusher, a 1 MVA dry-type transformer with fire detection and suppression for the main shaft winders, high-capacity remotely operated pumps at 11 mRL, IoT sensors on 11 critical equipment items and 28 Machine Max sensors; at Zawar, a 500 KW exhaust fan at Central Baroi lifting air capacity by 150 m3/s to 450 m3/s, the first remote surface operation of an underground pump at Mochia, Hindustan Zinc's longest raise of 600.2 m at Balaria, hydro filling at Balaria that will raise tailings utilisation from 17% to 25%, a shift to bulk emulsion charging, and new ore production from the Rawa area and 9E lens in the Mochia-Balaria cluster; and at Kayad, two ventilation fans (132 kW at +250 mRL and 450 kW at +120 mRL) boosting airflow by 150 m3/s. The rupee quantum of the programme is not narrated in this bundle; the only stated figures are the capital-commitment disclosures in the accounts.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Precise and willing to be pinned to numbers — 1.1mn tonnes was described as "our commitment," the 650KT capex was given as an honest straight-line extrapolation with the caveat that tendering would refine it, and the REE timeline was set at 2031–32 rather than sold as a near-term story. Arun Misra corrected two analyst framings cleanly: that the company had changed its no-concentrate-sale policy (it had not — this was legacy off-grade stock), and that the whole fertilizer plant commissions in Q2 (only phosphoric acid does). The RPT explanation was unusually transparent. Outgoing-CEO tone was valedictory; the CEO-designate did not speak on the call, which leaves the strategy-continuity question open.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Structural cost leadership - first quartile of the global zinc mining cost curve and first decile of the global zinc smelting cost curve; FY2026 zinc cost of production (ex-royalty) of US$ 959 per tonne was a five-year low, better 9% YoY in dollar terms
- Full integration from ore body to end product and from captive power generation to customer delivery, so an advantage created in one part of the value chain reinforces the next
- Irreplaceable asset base - highest-ever ore R&R of 468.6 Mnt at an average zinc-lead grade of 6.2%, highest-ever metal reserve of 13.9 Mnt since the underground transition and record silver reserves of 10.9 kt, supporting 25+ years of mine life; world's 2nd largest zinc and lead reserves and resources base
- Dominant domestic position - India's only integrated and only primary zinc producer, with c.74% expected primary zinc market share and 600 kt of domestic zinc sales in FY2026
- India's only primary zinc alloy producer and only listed primary precious metal (silver) company, with value-added products at c.22% of sales (184 kt) and over 20x silver production growth over two decades
- Captive power with a rising renewable share - c.18% of the power mix from renewables in FY2026 and domestic coal use raised to 53%, insulating power cost from commodity price variation
- Industry-leading profitability cited by management - EBITDA margin of c.54% backed by operational excellence, technology, cost optimisation and better by-product realisation; c.67% return on capital employed and c.77% return on equity
- Consistently AAA credit rating by CRISIL, supporting funding for the growth phase
- Product and sustainability differentiation - EcoZen, Asia's first low-carbon zinc brand at under 1 tCO2e per tonne, commercially scaled in FY2026 with MoUs signed with Tata Steel and Silox India Limited
- Market-access and pricing transparency edge - 95% of sales through online price discovery in FY2026 against a 100% ambition, plus the January 2026 launch of Zinc Moolya, a rupee-linked live pricing module aimed at MSMEs
- ESG leadership as a commercial asset - ranked 1st in S&P Global CSA for the third consecutive year, first Indian member of ICMM, and Zinc Mark / Copper Mark certified sites
- Precious metals contributed c.45% of overall profitability, giving a second earnings engine alongside zinc
- Technology-led exploration - AI/ML targeting, drone-based surveys and 3D deposit modelling supporting continuous R&R replenishment
- Recognition by the market - inclusion in Nifty 100, Nifty Next 50 and the NSE F&O segment, and in the Nifty100 ESG, Nifty100 Enhanced ESG and Nifty100 ESG Sector Leaders indices

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Leadership transition.** Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash (ex-SAIL CMD, 30+ years in steel) on 1 August 2026; the CFO, Amit Gupta, is also newly appointed. A new CEO arrives precisely as a ~INR24,000cr capex decision reaches the board — strategy continuity is unproven.
- **Coal linkage failure.** 36% domestic linkage vs 64% a quarter ago is a real, unhedged cost exposure.
- **No hedging in FY27.** Management is deliberately unhedged given volatility; carried-forward positions (48kt zinc @ USD3,162, 34t silver @ USD63) sit well below spot, so they cost INR200cr in Q1 and will keep bleeding while prices stay high — but the unhedged book leaves earnings fully exposed to a price reversal.
- **Silver price moderation.** Silver fell to USD73/oz from the prior quarter's strong levels while contributing 46% of profit — the single largest earnings sensitivity.
- **SEBI observations on related-party transactions.** No penalty or restriction, but corrective measures were required. Root cause disclosed candidly: omnibus RPT approvals are set on *value*, and operating teams track *volume*, so a rising LME can breach the approved value. New SOP triggers an alarm at 80% of approved value with escalation to the Audit Committee.
- **GoI stake sale speculation.** Media reports of the government selling its ~27.92%; management deflected — "it is for the government to give the update."
- **Fertilizer plant regulatory risk.** Environmental clearance still pending; the Q1 FY28 date is contingent on it.
- **Silver WIP.** 10–15t of silver sitting in work-in-progress inflates the apparent Q1 shortfall against the 680t guide; if it does not unlock, the annual target is at risk.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The prepared remarks and the Q&A disagree on the fertilizer plant: the opening script said the Chanderiya fertilizer plant was "on track to be completed by the second quarter," while the CEO later said only phosphoric acid completes in Q2 and fertilizer slips to Q1 FY28. Take the Q&A version — and treat the script as evidence that timeline discipline needs watching under the new CEO.
- Sulphuric acid is doing quiet, structural work: prices up ~200% YoY, netted off COP, and royalty-free — it is simultaneously depressing reported COP *and* depressing royalty as a percentage of revenue. A normalisation in acid prices would hit the P&L twice over.
- The concentrate sale is the cleanest read on management's opportunism: rather than derate smelters with off-grade material, they sold legacy stock into a high-LME market for INR315cr. But they flagged they will *not* repeat it if it risks starving the smelters — so this revenue line should disappear.
- Q1 at 260kt against a 1.1mn tonne guide is already 1,040kt annualised, i.e. the guidance carries a built-in buffer that Q2–Q4 seasonality (Q4 typically 280–290kt) should comfortably clear. The guide looks conservative rather than stretched.
- Silver at 46% of profitability means this is no longer usefully modelled as a zinc company.
